facts.text: AirSimDroneEnv is a gym.Env subclass; its constructor takes ip_address, image_shape, env_config and input_mode and connects an airsim.MultirotorClient to ip_address
The action space is a two-element Box with low -0.6, high 0.6 and dtype float32
The observation space is Box(0, 255) with dtype uint8; for multi_rgb its shape is (image_shape[0], image_shape[1]*3, 1), otherwise image_shape
The environment is registered as airsim-env-v0 with entry point scripts:AirSimDroneEnv
step calls do_action, get_obs and compute_reward and returns the legacy four values obs, reward, done, info
do_action sends moveByVelocityBodyFrameAsync(0.4, action[0], action[1], duration=1) and then moveByVelocityAsync(0, 0, 0, duration=1)
The AirSim duration argument is in seconds

setup_flight resets the drone, enables API control, arms it, commands moveToZAsync(-1, 1), stores the collision timestamp, chooses a random section, and sets the pose with y_pos and z_pos from ((np.random.rand(1,2)-0.5)*2)
The alignment reward is exp(-target_dist_curr_3d)*30; a collision or a lost hole gives -100 and done, and travelling more than 3.7 gives done
is_collision compares the current simGetCollisionInfo().time_stamp with the timestamp stored at setup
get_obs for depth requests a DepthPerspective image, clips values above 3.4 and scales the clipped value by 255/3.4
The README gives the input sizes as 50 x 50 x 1 for depth, 50 x 50 x 3 for single RGB and 50 x 150 x 1 for stacked gray
The README says the project currently runs only on Windows because the Unreal environments are packaged for Windows
The README says the training scene is a separately downloaded TrainEnv.zip and its executable must be opened before training
config.yml sets train_mode and test_mode to multi_rgb
train.py builds image_shape (50,50,1) for depth and (50,50,3) otherwise and calls gym.make('scripts:airsim-env-v0', ip_address='127.0.0.1', image_shape=..., env_config=..., input_mode=...)
The README's settings.json configures a 50 x 50 camera with FOV_Degrees 120 and ClockSpeed 40

determinism.notes: the fake draws its initial y and z from random.Random(seed) and its transitions are deterministic, so reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 repeats a trajectory on the fake; the upstream reset takes no seed and the external AirSim scene was not run

gaps: the fake is a kinematic corridor stand-in: positions advance by the commanded body-frame velocity for the 1 s command period, with no Unreal renderer, no AirSim physics, no contacts and no actuator, sensor or noise model

the upstream environment runs only on Windows and needs the separately downloaded TrainEnv.zip Unreal/AirSim executable (README.md:8 and :165-171); the sim backend was not run and the fake was never compared with the upstream scene
the observation is the configured 50 x 50 x 1 depth array (train.py:22-24), but the fake paints a synthetic depth grid with a target marker instead of rendering the Unreal camera
the AirSim physics timestep is not in the clone; one tick is one 1 s velocity command (scripts/airsim_env.py:87-88), so timestep_ms describes the fake's command period only
no snapshot or restore: AirSimDroneEnv exposes no get_state or set_state
the fake accepts reset options start, target and sections for deterministic tests; AirSimDroneEnv.reset takes no options (scripts/airsim_env.py:42-45)
the bridge is configured autoreset=True, so a step after a terminal state starts a new episode; AirSimDroneEnv itself expects the caller to call reset()

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
